title: The Plain Email Checklist: Send Cold Emails With Zero Links
description: A pre-send checklist for plain cold emails: no links, no images, tracking off, matched inboxes, and a text opt-out. Plus the reply to send when they ask.
lead: This is the full plain email checklist from the reel. Spam filters look hard at email from strangers, and often it's the extras that get you flagged: links, images and tracking. This guide shows how to strip your first email down, what to do instead of a link, and how to check every email before it goes out.
insider: Our first emails for clients go out like this: plain text, no links, tracking off. Over one full quarter, a campaign of ours sent **236,545 emails at a 3.69% reply rate**. Cleaning up one email is easy. Keeping thousands of emails and inboxes clean every day is what we do for clients.

blocks.text: Why the extras get you in trouble

A cold email comes from someone the reader has never emailed. Spam filters are extra careful with those. Links, images and tracking codes are things marketing emails and scams use a lot, so they add risk to a message that already has none of the trust of a known sender.
A plain email looks like what it should be: one person writing to another.
What the data says

items: **Tracking costs replies.** In [Hunter's State of Email Outreach 2026](https://hunter.io/the-state-of-cold-email) (31 million emails), sequences with tracking on got **4.4% replies vs 7.4% with it off**.

**Open tracking is a hidden image.** [Hunter explains](https://hunter.io/cold-email-guide/email-tracking) that an open-tracking pixel is "an invisible image" added to the email, and that some spam filters may block emails with tracking pixels or tracked links.

**Zero links is the safe default.** [lemlist's guidance](https://help.lemlist.com/en/articles/13941647-lemcoach-should-you-track-clicks-and-opens-in-cold-email-campaigns) says to limit links to 1 per email, "ideally 0 in your initial cold outreach", and that untracked links show better deliverability than tracked ones.

**Images aren't a magic fix either way.** Hunter found images and attachments did not measurably change reply rates. So there's little upside to adding them, and they push the email toward looking like marketing.

blocks.label: Be honest with yourself
blocks.text: A plain email gets you a fair chance at the inbox. It won't save a bad message. The words still have to be short and about them.

Run every first email through this before it goes live.

blocks.text: How to set it up, step by step

items: **Write in plain text.** In your sending tool, pick the plain text option, or paste from a plain text editor so no hidden formatting comes along.
**Remove every link from email 1.** That includes your website, your calendar link and social links in the signature.
**Clean the signature.** Name, title, company. That's it. If you type your website, many email apps will turn it into a link, so leave it out of email 1.
**Turn off open tracking and click tracking** in the campaign settings. Measure replies instead. Replies are the number that matters.

**Turn on provider matching** if your tool has it. [Instantly](https://help.instantly.ai/en/articles/7044069-email-service-providers-matching), for example, sends from an account with the same provider as the recipient, such as Google to Google.
**Add a text opt-out line** at the bottom.
**Send a test to yourself** on both a Gmail and an Outlook address. Check it arrives in the main inbox and looks like a normal email.

blocks.text: Let them ask for the link
Instead of a link, offer the thing in words. When they reply "sure, send it", that's a reply, which is what you want. Then you send the link in your answer, to someone who asked for it.

head: With a link (avoid in email 1)
Without a link
rows: "Want me to send the case study?"
"Open to a quick call Thursday at 10?"
"Happy to send a 1-page overview if it's useful."
"I made a 2-minute video of your site with 3 fixes. Want it?"

blocks.label: Reply when they ask for the link
blocks.text:
Hi [first name],

Here you go: [link]

The part most useful for you is [section], since [one reason tied to their company].

Want me to walk you through it Thursday at 10?

[your name]
Where links can go later

items: **In your replies**, once they ask for something. A link in a conversation they started is normal.
**In a later follow-up**, if you must, and only one. Keep it plain (no tracking) and on a domain that matches your sending domain.
**Never** a link shortener like bit.ly. Short links hide where they go, which is what scammers do.

blocks.text: Stay legal without an unsubscribe link

You still have to let people opt out. The [FTC's CAN-SPAM guide](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business) allows a return email address as the opt-out method, so "reply and I'll stop" can work in the US. It also requires your valid physical postal address in the email and that you honor opt-outs within 10 business days. Other countries have their own rules, so check the law where your buyers are.

[Google's sender guidelines](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/81126) ask senders of marketing and subscribed messages to support one-click unsubscribe, and bulk senders (over 5,000 messages a day to Gmail) to keep their spam rate under 0.3%. Keep your newsletters and marketing emails on the normal unsubscribe link.

blocks.text: Clean up your email with Claude

blocks.label: Plain email prompt
blocks.text:
Here is my cold email:
[paste email, including signature]

Rewrite it as a plain first email:
- Remove every link, image and attachment, including from the signature
- If the email points to a link (case study, video, calendar), replace it with a one-line offer to send it, e.g. "Want me to send it?"
- Under 80 words, short sentences, about their problem, one clear ask
- Signature: name, title, company only
- End with: "Reply 'no thanks' and I won't email again."
Then list every change you made.

blocks.label: The rule
blocks.text: No links, no images, no tracking. Let them ask.

faq.q: Then how do I measure if the email works?
faq.a: Count replies and positive replies. Opens are unreliable anyway, because some apps and security bots load images automatically.

faq.q: Can I put a link in a follow-up email?
faq.a: You can, but keep it to one, untracked, on your own domain. Many people keep all links for the reply, after the person asks.

faq.q: What if my tool doesn't do provider matching?
faq.a: Then focus on the rest of the checklist. Matching helps, but plain text, no tracking and a good list matter more.
In the US, CAN-SPAM allows a return email address as the opt-out method, plus your physical address in the email. Rules differ by country, so check where your buyers are.
